A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeFilter. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison, including material shifted by pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on 13 datasets, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and prediction examples in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds DUET results to the fixed-input long-term and short-term comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same patch graph construction, three dependency filters, dynamic Top-p routing, graph aggregation, prediction procedure, and training losses. Added citations and wording changes do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine long-term datasets and four PEMS short-term datasets. The represented forecasting tasks, domains, and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: DUET is added to the fixed-input long-term comparisons in Tables 1 and 8 and short-term comparisons in Tables 3 and 10. It already participated in the longer-input comparison in Tables 2 and 9 and the efficiency analysis. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 changes the printed MSE and MAE summation lower bounds from i=1 to 0 while retaining upper bound T and normalization by T. This changes the documented formulas, but does not establish changed metric implementations or recomputation. Splits, forecasting horizons, model settings, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The filtering and MoE ablations in Tables 4 and 11, dependency analysis in Figure 4, horizon and efficiency analyses in Figures 5–6, and prediction examples in Figures 7–10 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 retains three experimental repetitions, the standard deviations in Table 7, and the Wilcoxon comparison with Leddam reporting p=4.66e-10 and 99% confidence. No new uncertainty procedure accompanies the DUET entries.

E6.justification: DUET result entries are added while shared model scores remain unchanged. On PEMS08, DUET's MSE/MAE of 0.096/0.192 makes TimeFilter's reported margins 13.54%/3.13%, replacing 18.63%/11.85% against Leddam. DUET also becomes best on Solar-Energy MAE, scoring 0.233 against TimeFilter's unchanged 0.250.

T1.justification: The changed summation bounds in Appendix A.2 constitute a small, mathematically non-equivalent edit to the metric definitions: starting at 0 while ending at T and dividing by T introduces an apparent indexing inconsistency. The method equations and other mathematical content are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction lowers the claimed short-term error reduction from 8.02% to 5.34%, retaining the 4.48% long-term claim. The central novelty, patch-specific dependency modeling, and overall state-of-the-art claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning noisy dependencies, spurious relationships, dataset-specific filtering, longer inputs, and efficiency remain unchanged. The added generic Impact Statement supplies no substantive new limitation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A retain the same software, GPU, optimizer, hyperparameter choices, batch sizes, epoch counts, dataset descriptions, and code access information. No additional implementation instructions accompany the new comparator results.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven cited works, including three graph sparsification references explicitly connected to routing and four forecasting or data-related references in the dataset discussion. The broader CI/CD/CC positioning and related-work structure remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, wording and cross-references are edited, and 'Methodology' becomes 'Method.' Affiliations and publication information are updated, and acknowledgements and an Impact Statement are added. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 3, 8, and 10 gain DUET columns and updated ranking highlights. Figure 1 is restyled and its caption explains DTW; several figures are resized or reformatted. The existing figures and tables are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Adding DUET under the fixed-input and short-term settings closes a specific gap in comparisons against channel clustering, a central target of the paper's motivation. Updated margins reflect the stronger comparator, and presentation receives modest clarification. These benefits outweigh the small mathematical inconsistency introduced in Appendix A.2; the method and existing experimental evidence otherwise remain stable.
